
### files in building C programs [dynamic linking] 


::: {.r-stack .my-full}

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-dynamic-linking.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Dependency diagram showing source files main.c, main.h, extra.h, stdio.h, extra.c; main.o built from main.c, main.h, extra.h, stdio.h; extra.o built from extra.c, extra.h; and program (an executable) built from main.o, extra.o and system files. The program is shown to load libc.so at runtime."}

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-dynamic-linking.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Same diagram as before, with the production of main.o and extra.o highlighted and showing that the commands 'clang -c main.c' and 'clang -c extra.c' are used."}

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-dynamic-linking.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="Same diagram as before, but instead of showing the the .o files (main.o, extra.o) being produced from the .c and .h files directly, they are produced from a .s file (like 'main.s') which is produced from the .c and .h files. The commands 'clang -S -c main.c' and 'clang -S -c extra.c' are shown to do these steps."}

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-dynamic-linking.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 fig-alt="Same daigram as before with the step producing the program from .o files and system files highlighted and  showing the command 'clang -o program main.o extra.o'."}

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-dynamic-linking.figure-5.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=5 fig-alt="Same diagram as before, highlighting running running the program with ./program and this loading libc.so at runtime."}

:::


### files in building C programs [static linking] 

![](/building/texfig/c-file-types-files-in-building-c-programs-static-linking.figure.svg){fig-alt="same dependency diagram as previous slide, but instead of loading libc.so at runtime, the program is built using libc.a in addition to other files"}


### file extensions  {.smaller}

<table class="collines rowlines">
<tr><td>name</td><td>&nbsp;</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.h</code></td><td></td><td>C header file</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.s</code></td><td>(or <code>.asm</code>)</td><td>assembly file</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>.o</code></td><td>(or <code>.obj</code>)</td><td>object file (binary of assembly)</td></tr>
<tr><td>(none)</td><td>(or <code>.exe</code>)</td><td>executable file</td></tr>
<tr><td>.a</td><td>(or <code>.lib</code>)</td><td>statically linked libraryi<br/>(collection of .o files)</td></tr>
<tr><td>.so</td><td>(or <code>.dll</code> or <code>.dylib</code>)</td><td>dynamically linked library<br/>('shared object')</td></tr>
</table>
